_note: Campaign chapters. Goals are checked by js/game/campaign.js. Events are scripted set pieces.

chapters.title: The Garage
chapters.story: 1995. You lease a cage in an old print works with a Cisco 2514, a Catalyst 1924 and a dream. The web is new and everyone wants a homepage.

chapters.title: Dot-com Boom
chapters.story: Venture capital is raining from the sky. Startups need racks yesterday. Build a proper core and keep the lights on.

chapters.title: The Worm Year
chapters.story: January 2003. A tiny UDP worm is about to saturate links around the world. Firewalls are no longer optional.

chapters.title: 10 Gigabit & Redundancy
chapters.story: Virtualisation means every rack is busy. Customers want 99.99% and they read their SLAs.

goals.text: Run a redundant core pair (HSRP/VRRP + LACP)

chapters.title: The Leap Second
chapters.story: 30 June 2012, 23:59:60. Somewhere a kernel is about to spin on a futex.

goals.text: Open the office floor with Wi-Fi

chapters.title: Patch Tuesday Forever
chapters.story: April 2014. Heartbleed has every security team awake. Your patch calendar is about to matter.

chapters.title: Dual-Homed
chapters.story: Customers ask about your upstream diversity. Get your own ASN, a second ISP and BGP.

goals.text: Connect a second ISP over BGP

chapters.title: The Route Leak
chapters.story: An upstream is about to send you the entire internet routing table. Hope you set your limits.

chapters.title: Hyperscale
chapters.story: 400G optics, Junos Evolved and infrastructure as code. Build the empire.

slammer.title: SQL Slammer outbreak
slammer.text: A worm on UDP 1434 is flooding the internet. Your transit links are saturating. Block UDP 1434 at the edge (ACL or firewall policy).

leapsecond.title: Leap second
leapsecond.text: After the leap second, customer servers are burning 100% CPU. On each affected server: date -s "$(date)"

heartbleed.title: Heartbleed disclosed
heartbleed.text: A critical OpenSSL bug is public. Every device and server with a TLS management interface must be patched.

routeleak.title: Upstream route leak
routeleak.text: An ISP starts announcing the full table. Sessions without a sensible maximum-prefix will choke - or ones with a tiny limit will drop.
